analysis.title: Where Have All the Volumes Gone? SPY Volume Lowest in Two Decades
key_insights: SPY volume on Friday (10/9/26) was 22.6M shares, the lowest since 12/24/19 (a half-day). Among full trading days it is the lowest since 11/25/05, and among days not bordering market holidays the lowest since 10/11/04.
Monday 10/12 was on pace for about 19M SPY shares, which would be the lowest non-holiday volume since 2003.
BTIG attributes the low volume mainly to the calendar: a lull between major macro catalysts and earnings season, with investors waiting for banks to report later in the week.
Broader volume is less extreme. NYSE Composite volume on Friday was below its 20-day average but above August levels.

One-day volume extremes, especially on the low side, are hard to use. A volume surge after a decline is the useful capitulation signal for contrarian entries, as seen in Software in April and Semis in late July.
The 5-day moving average of SPY volume was likely to finish Monday near 31M. Since 2005 it has been below 35M only three other times: early Dec 2024, mid-Feb 2025 and late Aug 2026.

After the Dec 2024 low, SPY fell 5% into mid-January, then rallied to a marginal new high. After the mid-Feb 2025 low, which was the peak before the liberation day decline, SPY fell 21%. After the late Aug 2026 low, SPY had a modest 2.9% pullback into mid-September.

Index volatility is also unusually low. The SPX has gone 52 trading days without a -1% down day, tying the streak that ended in July 2024. One more day would make it the longest since Jan 2020 (74 days).
There has been no 80%+ downside volume day on the NYSE in nearly a year, the longest streak since at least 1996 by a wide margin.

Bottom line: low volume and low volatility are weak timing tools, but each of the prior three low-volume periods saw SPY weaken shortly after. BTIG expects both volume and volatility to pick up as earnings season gets going.
earnings_insights: Bank earnings begin later in the week of 10/12/26 and are cited as the next catalyst. BTIG expects volume and volatility to rise as earnings season gets going. No EPS or revenue figures are given.
risk_factors: Low-volume, low-volatility regimes in Dec 2024, Feb 2025 and Aug 2026 were each followed by SPY weakness. The Feb 2025 case preceded a 21% decline.
Volume and volatility are expected to rise as earnings season begins, which could end the calm.
